context: First inventory current chart rendering, result-file containment, tenant workspace roots, supported formats, artifact publication, and cleanup behavior. Choose an explicit response contract for inline content versus an opaque tenant-owned artifact handle/path; reject unsupported formats and traversal; never let caller-selected output_dir escape the server-owned chart root or leak another tenant. Preserve ASCII default compatibility. If file output is not justified for the supported MCP contract, document the intentional omission and close the item with evidence instead of adding a second publication model.
description: Successor of add-file-output-support-to-mcp-chart-generation, promoted from deferral #523 of visualization-suggestions-and-render-orchestration. BenchBox MCP currently returns inline ASCII from generate_chart and accepts output_dir only as a reserved, unused argument. Define whether and how remote clients may request durable chart files, then implement the smallest safe contract if approved. This is separate from the stateless transport migration but affects remote MCP usability.

preserves.behavior: Inline ASCII output and the existing generate_chart default remain backward compatible
No bearer token, raw database URL, unbounded argument, or result payload is emitted into telemetry or shared cache
Output paths stay inside server-owned tenant chart roots and cannot cross tenants or escape by traversal
Unsupported formats and unsafe output requests fail closed with structured MCP errors

verifications.description: The output contract is specified and guarded by a regression marker

verifications.description: Visualization unit tests cover safe output behavior
verifications.expected: exits 1 on an unfixed tree if the approved output contract is absent or unsafe; exits 0 once the focused suite passes

work_units.summary: Revalidate current generate_chart behavior, output_dir handling, chart-root containment, tenant ownership, formats, and artifact retention
Specify the remote file-output response, authorization, path-containment, format, overwrite, retention, and error semantics or document the intentional inline-only decision
Implement the approved safe contract across MCP schemas, visualization handlers, and durable artifact publication without changing ASCII default behavior
Add traversal, cross-tenant, overwrite, format, artifact-lifecycle, and transport tests plus reference documentation
